daily.title: From cotton mills to cityscapes – How the Singhanias are unlocking legacy land
daily.summary: The 104-year-old JK group company is betting on a ₹965-crore hospitality push and a ₹4,400-crore real estate pipeline built on its old industrial land Over a century ago, JK Cotton spun textiles out of Kanpur, before the company diversified into other businesses. Renamed JK Urbanscapes in 2023, the 104-year-old company, which attempted a brief revival of its textile business in 2009, is now betting on a bigger prize: turning old industrial and mill land into hospitality and urban real estate.

daily.title: SEBI starts work on network to train independent directors
daily.summary: SEBI begins building a network with industry and academia to train independent directors amid rising startup and IPO activity. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has started working on a wider capacity-building network to train and upgrade the skills of independent directors, bringing together professional industry bodies and academic institutions to develop programmes aimed at improving boardroom oversight, according to people familiar with the developments. The discussions centred on how the institutions could collaborate on developing training programmes, sharing expertise and creating a wider pool of resources for independent directors.

daily.title: CBIC Proposes Changes to Section 16 and New Section 16A to Protect Genuine ITC Claims
daily.summary: CBIC proposes changes to Section 16 & new Section 16A to protect genuine ITC claims, aiming to prevent penalising recipients for supplier defaults. The proposal seeks to bring greater clarity to ITC eligibility and ensure that bona fide recipients are not penalised merely because of defaults committed by suppliers or other persons in the supply chain. At the same time, it aims to prevent taxpayers knowingly involved in fraudulent transactions from claiming ITC. The proposals form part of an agenda note prepared by the GST Policy Wing of CBIC following deliberations at the 57th GST Council meeting.

daily.title: Nepal PM visit: India weighs $2-billion development package for Kathmandu
daily.summary: India weighs up to $2B Kathmandu package tied to DPRs and progress, with focus on infrastructure, energy, connectivity, and new cooperation areas. India is favourably considering Nepal’s proposal for up to $2 billion in grants and credit, with some project announcements likely during Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s two-day visit, which begins on Sunday. However, Kathmandu may have to submit detailed project reports before funds are sanctioned, with disbursements likely to be linked to project progress and utilisation, sources said.

daily.title: Asia, Africa to drive expansion of India's export markets as shipments grow across regions
daily.summary: India's merchandise exports have shown strong growth, particularly in Africa and Asia, according to recent government data. Exports to Africa increased by 44 percent, while shipments to Asia surpassed USD 100 billion. Engineering goods, electronic goods, and petroleum products have driven this expansion significantly. Notable growth was observed in markets such as Tanzania and Kenya in Africa.

daily.title: South Korea prepares market stabilisation funds after KOSPI hits 10-month low
daily.summary: In response to falling stock indices, South Korea's finance ministry is poised to activate market stabilisation funds. The KOSPI index has plummeted, marking its lowest point in the last ten months. An emergency meeting was convened by the finance minister to explore strategies for restoring investor confidence. Among the discussed actions are temporary regulations on stock buyback limits for publicly listed companies.

daily.title: Crude oil futures brace for OPEC+ output decision amid supply glut concerns: Analysts

daily.title: Rising government debt unlikely to trigger broad sovereign crisis in 2027: UBS
daily.summary: Government borrowing and debt-servicing costs are likely to escalate challenges for major economies by 2027. UBS reports that pressure stems from refinanced debt from low interest rates previously. Factors contributing to public finance pressure include ageing populations and entitlement spending. Measures like bond buybacks and changes in debt issuance strategies can help manage financing pressures. Nonetheless, UBS warns about potential difficulties that could lead to a debt crisis.

Road Tax Exemption for Disabled Persons Cannot Be Restricted by Statute: Madras HC
daily.summary: Madras HC directs fresh road tax exemption notification for disabled persons, considering unadapted vehicles and safeguards against misuse. At the same time, the Court recognised the possibility of misuse if exemption were granted without safeguards. Vehicles could be registered in the names of persons with disabilities but used by others, or transferred shortly after purchase. Referring to earlier guidelines governing GST concession certificates for persons with orthopaedic disabilities , the Court identified possible safeguards relating to vehicle specifications, disability certification, income tax returns, declarations concerning previous concessions and restrictions on disposal of vehicles.

daily.title: GSTAT Bengaluru Restores 100% Penalty for Suppressed Turnover Detected During GST Audit
daily.summary: GSTAT Bengaluru restores ₹22.62 lakh GST penalties, holding that audit-triggered disclosure cannot defeat Section 74 suppression proceedings. Summary : The GST Appellate Tribunal, Bengaluru , in Pallawi Anand Vs Sadhana Enviro Engineering Services , allowed the Revenue’s appeal against an appellate order that had deleted or reduced penalties arising from GST audit discrepancies for FY 2018–19. The dispute concerned two distinct categories of tax liability: ₹34,69,134 representing outward tax disclosed in GSTR-1 but not paid through GSTR-3B , and ₹19,02,658 relating to additional taxable receipts and liabilities that came to light through audit scrutiny .

daily.title: GST Order Set Aside as SCN Reply and Hearing Dates Were Same: Allahabad HC
daily.summary: Allahabad HC sets aside GST ITC demand where SCN reply and hearing dates coincided; remands matter subject to ₹5,000 costs. Summary : The Allahabad High Court considered a writ petition filed by M/s Kanha Mentha Traders challenging a GST assessment order dated 4 January 2022 and an appellate order dated 30 April 2026 dismissing its appeal on the ground of delay. The petitioner, a partnership firm engaged in the Mentha Oil business, had purchased goods valued at ₹55,26,000 from M/s Vishnu Traders and claimed input tax credit of ₹6,63,120, comprising CGST and SGST of ₹3,31,560 each.

daily.title: Ahead of FY28 budget, aluminium product makers seek duty-free imports for primary metal
daily.summary: Ahead of the Union budget for 2027-28, aluminium product manufacturers have urged the government to allow duty-free imports of raw metal to boost domestic consumption and enhance the competitiveness of small enterprises. Manufacturers' body ALEMAI has written a letter to Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, seeking to bring down the basic customs duty on primary aluminium to zero, arguing that the current 7.5 per cent levy, which translates into an effective import duty of 8.25 per cent including social welfare surcharge, is hurting MSMEs (micro, small and medium enterprises) and domestic value addition.

daily.title: CBIC Issues Detailed Guidelines for Implementation of Diamond Imprest Authorisation Scheme: Clarifies 12-Month Import Validity, 18-Month Export Obligation, 10% Value Addition and Customs Duty Exemption
daily.summary: The Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC), Ministry of Finance, Government of India, has issued Circular No. 48/2026-Customs dated November 20, The Circular has been issued to ensure uniform implementation of the Scheme by Customs field formations and to clarify the eligibility conditions, import restrictions, export obligations, documentation requirements, security arrangements and procedures for regularisation of defaults. The Scheme provides for duty-exempt imports of eligible natural cut and polished diamonds against a prescribed obligation to undertake physical exports of natural cut and polished diamonds with minimum value addition.
